title: Sharp Risk Constants for Restricted Mean Survival Time in the Supercritical Regime
banked_reason: Typed D0.5 kernel_substituted: the requested all-rule equality, certified evaluable constant and original-record attainment remain open; independent main validity audit confirms no bounded faithful repair. Companion mathematics and all five cited leaves pass.
tldr: The finite original-record compiler returns computable \(C_\chi,n_\chi\) and unconditionally gives the fixed-specification comparison error \(C_\chi(A_n^{1/2}+n^{-1})\le C_\chi b_n\) on the full primitive class. Computable dyadic block starts give a growing cofinal resolution sequence with vanishing risk discrepancy. Fixed finite compiler rules have \(O(n^{-12/13})\) squared risk, and a zero-table compiler family gives an explicit local upper envelope. Quantitative convergence of decision-game values, radius-preserving remote gluing, information-leakage control and equality or evaluation of \(C_-\) and \(C_+\) remain unresolved.
gap: Finite-profile likelihood limits do not control the squared risks of observable nonlinear RMST rules over a full primitive class. Positive-retention survival inference and known-base scalar density comparison leave different proof obligations at this marked endpoint.
fill: The theorem supplies a computable full-class error bound for every finite correction table, including training-selected tables, and a complete-likelihood finite-prior lower comparison. Relative to \texttt{\detokenize{stat_rmst_cubic_logexperiment/v1}}, the increment is quantitative finite-decision risk transport beyond a matched exponent, rather than evaluation of the unrestricted constant.
